3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I had a meeting scheduled with Paskal to receive the annual healthcare report.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: He arrived at my office with stacks of papers underneath both arms.

7.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
7.text: “I know this seems like a lot.”

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: He put the mountain of papers on my desk. It made a loud thud sound.

10.speaker: Player
10.text: “Very well. Thanks for bringing these in.”

11.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
11.text: “Reviewing it shouldn't take more than a day.”

15.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
15.text: “They contain very important information about the status of our healthcare.”

21.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
21.text: “But I don't want to bore you. So I will quickly summarize.”

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: I breathed a sigh of relief as he put on his reading glasses to look at the document he was holding.

24.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
24.text: “So, we have concluded our report for the year.”

31.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
31.text: “We have more patients treated, less waiting times and higher treatment quality than the years before.”

35.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
35.text: “We have missed several funding opportunities to expand our services in the country, leading to several issues being unsolved.”

36.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
36.text: “We are certainly on the right path to challenge even Lespia or Valgsland in the matter but we are not there yet.”

37.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
37.text: “I couldn't agree more. The foundations we laid so far will influence the years to come.”

38.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
38.text: “There can't be a more valiant aim. The foundations we laid so far will influence the years to come.”

39.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
39.text: “The service quality has dropped across the country. We have longer waiting times, fewer doctors and nurses, and more areas without proper healthcare.”

40.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
40.text: “Thanks to the allocated funds from the state, we have improved the healthcare in the country overall. I have used the resources to begin a comprehensive health reform.”

41.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
41.text: “Our services haven't necessarily gotten better compared to the last years.”

42.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
42.text: “The health services have been downsized and cut according to the new budget plan which caused a negative impact.”

43.speaker: Player
43.text: “That is great to hear. Thank you for your hard work, Paskal.”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “Just as I expected. It was a good decision to spend the budget on the healthcare.”

45.speaker: Player
45.text: “Good. Under my Presidency, I want Sordish people to have the best health service they can get.”

46.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
46.text: “This wouldn't be possible without your wise decision, Mr. President. So, thank you.”

47.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
47.text: “However, give it a few more years and we might even surpass them.”

48.speaker: Player
48.text: “We need to get to the level of superpowers.”

49.speaker: Player
49.text: “We can't simply follow the footsteps of other nations.”

52.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
52.text: “I agree. We need to pave our own path to a better healthcare for our citizens.”

53.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
53.text: “It will take effort. However, if we can stay for another term, I am sure we will.”

55.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
55.text: “Our privatization efforts had both positive and negative effects.”

56.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
56.text: “It helped us raise further funds that we spent on improving the system. Privatized hospitals opened in many places with top notch equipment.”

57.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
57.text: “But, on the other hand, privatized hospitals are rather expensive even for an ordinary middle-class citizen.”

58.speaker: Player
58.text: “We should be able to serve all of our citizens without distinction.”

59.speaker: Player
59.text: “These are the expected growing pains of our healthcare system.”

60.speaker: Player
60.text: “There are still public hospitals for lower-class citizens.”

61.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
61.text: “One of the side effects of a privatised healthcare system.”

62.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
62.text: “We are doing that now thanks to the increased resources. However, there is still some disparity in terms of quality.”

63.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
63.text: “True. But, there is still some disparity in terms of quality.”

64.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
64.text: “I agree. Now, we need to look into the future.”

65.speaker: Narrator
65.text: Paskal skimmed the rest of the document before putting it down.

66.speaker: Player
66.text: “Anybody can succeed when given all the resources. We need to do better.”

67.speaker: Player
67.text: “Don't blame yourself. It was my decision.”

68.speaker: Player
68.text: “Then you need to do a better job, Paskal.”

69.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
69.text: “Yes. I agree. The recession absolutely pushed welfare to the brink and no further funds mean we couldn't do much.”

70.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
70.text: “We are in this together, Mr. President. The Ministry is trying to improve the efficiency where possible even in this situation. I assure you.”

71.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
71.text: “Yes, Mr. President. I will do my best even in these circumstances.”

72.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
72.text: “But as you can see, it hasn't been the best year for us at all.”

73.speaker: Player
73.text: “We will do better next year. Don't worry.”

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “Then get to the bottom of it.”

75.speaker: Player
75.text: “That is unfortunate but what is done is done.”

77.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
77.text: “That is what I am trying to achieve.”

78.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
78.text: “We should strive to do better in this avenue.”

79.speaker: Player
79.text: “Try to keep the problems to a minimum as best you can.”

80.speaker: Player
80.text: “During our next term we will re-evaluate the situation in health.”

82.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
82.text: “We are overwhelmed. Cutting the expenditures overboard has put us in a spiral of losing further incomes due to the lack of quality health services.”

83.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
83.text: “We must. If we have another year like this one, we might not be able to recover fully. Ever.”

84.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
84.text: “I understand however, the health of our citizens should be closer to the top of that list.”

85.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
85.text: “My team is absolutely exhausted, and all the fired personnel from the Ministry are furious with our administration.”

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “We will assess the situation and find solutions.”

89.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
89.text: “The situation is grave. We shouldn't underestimate it.”

90.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
90.text: “Yes, sure. But when one gets hit with the consequences of such sacrifices, it is hard to be happy about it.”

92.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
92.text: “Perhaps. But, I understand where their dissatisfaction comes from.”

108.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
108.text: “Our new funds allowed us to build dozens of new hospitals around the country. We specifically focused on areas with a high demand of health services.”

109.speaker: Player
109.text: “Great to hear that more citizens have access to hospitals.”

110.speaker: Player
110.text: “The people will see clear progress in the new hospitals we built.”

112.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
112.text: “Many citizens have already written letters to us, thanking for the new treatment possibilities and less waiting times.”

113.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
113.text: “Not just that, we have increased our overall bed count for patients which increased the treatment capacity in many hospitals.”

114.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
114.text: “Thank you. I try to do my best.”

115.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
115.text: “The quality of care increased due to the upgraded equipment and we were able to hire more healthcare staff.”

116.speaker: Player
116.text: “Excellent, the people in the countryside deserve better health services.”

117.speaker: Player
117.text: “Inequality is our worst enemy and we are one step closer to beating it.”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “Make sure they know that we were the ones who gave this to them.”

119.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
119.text: “There is no need. They already know.”

120.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
120.text: “The disparity in services needs more effort to be completely solved. However, the additional funds for the rural areas are a great start.”

121.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
121.text: “Yes. They have been neglected for a long time due to political reasons. Not anymore.”

122.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
122.text: “The investments we poured into our rural health facilities has paid off greatly.”

123.speaker: Player
123.text: “High morale and happiness will result in better service.”

124.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
124.text: “The act was the first of its kind, along with the salary incentives in rural areas which resulted in more job applications to areas that lacked health staff.”

125.speaker: Player
125.text: “Our doctors, nurses and other health workers deserved better.”

126.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
126.text: “We are already seeing the positive results. It is safe to assume that it was worth it.”

127.speaker: Player
127.text: “It better be worth the losses in capital.”

128.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
128.text: “The Ministry has been ecstatic about the changes. The departments have been singing your praises.”

129.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
129.text: “Surely. With the rural incentives we have more treatment quality in those areas as well.”

130.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
130.text: “The increase in salaries to all health workers was received very well.”
130.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_ImproveRural"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Hospitals"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Salary"] == true)

131.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
131.text: “All of these efforts have resulted in a clear improvement of access to health services for our citizens.”
131.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Hospitals"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_ImproveRural"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Hospitals"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Salary"] == true) == false)

132.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
132.text: “All these efforts have resulted in a clear increase of quality in health services provided to our citizens.”
132.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Hospitals"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_ImproveRural"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_ImproveRural"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Salary"] == true) == false)

133.speaker: Narrator
133.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Hospitals"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_ImproveRural"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Salary"] == true) == false)

134.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
134.text: “Now that I have given you the short summary...”

135.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
135.text: “There is a very important matter to discuss.”

136.speaker: Narrator
136.text: Leaning over to grab his briefcase, he pulled out a tan colored package. The package was stamped with big red letters that read 'Confidential'.

137.speaker: Narrator
137.text: Paskal opened the package and brought out a few documents. He handed them over to me.

139.speaker: Narrator
139.text: It was a report from the Ministry of Health. Each page had a stamp on it that read 'For The President's Eyes Only'.

140.speaker: Narrator
140.text: The report was titled 'Polio Outbreak in Bergia'.

144.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
144.text: “For now it seems to be under control. We have put a few villages under quarantine. The total number of infected is currently 1467. The death toll is at 23 so far.”

145.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
145.text: “If we have more outbreaks, the results will be terrible.”

147.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
147.text: “Do not underestimate diseases and plagues, Mr. President.”

154.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
154.text: “Thankfully we have received the additional funding to our healthcare.”

155.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
155.text: “This should curb the infection ratio. Although, I am afraid even that might not be enough.”

156.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
156.text: “We are not where we could have been in terms of our healthcare funding.”

157.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
157.text: “With what we currently have, I am afraid it might not be enough to curb the infection ratio.”

158.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
158.text: “With the funding cuts to our healthcare, we are in potentially very dangerous territory.”

159.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
159.text: “If the hospitals start overflowing, we will be done for.”

160.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
160.text: “I will tell it to you straight. With our current state, we can't even hope to curb the infection ration if there are more outbreaks.”

161.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
161.text: “This is a very serious matter, Mr. President. The lives of Sordish citizens are at stake.”

163.speaker: Player
163.text: “How bad can it be? Don't worry about it. It will stop. I know it.”

164.speaker: Player
164.text: “I will do whatever it takes to eliminate this threat.”

165.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
165.text: “Mr. President. I beg you to see reason.”

167.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
167.text: “With that attitude, I have no doubt that we will succeed.”

168.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
168.text: “But I'm afraid simply having the vaccines won't help. We need to make sure they are administered.”

169.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
169.text: “There is a cure. A vaccine was recently invented in United Contana, and the formula has been made available for free across the entire world.”

170.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
170.text: “No matter what people think about United Contana, if the same thing had happened in Arcasia, we would be paying a steep price for it.”

174.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
174.text: “Thanks to the very good decision made by you to increase funding for our healthcare, we have the capability to produce this vaccine locally.”

175.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
175.text: “Unfortunately, because of the state of our current funding, we have neither the required materials nor the capability to produce this vaccine locally.”

176.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
176.text: “Which means we have to buy it. It will be costly but nothing comes before health.”

177.speaker: Player
177.text: “You are exaggerating. There have been fewer than 30 deaths and you said the infected were under quarantine. I'm not going to approve this procurement.”

178.speaker: Player
178.text: “Procure whatever you need. Immediately. [-1 Government Budget]”

180.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
180.text: “Mr. President. You are knowingly exposing Sordland to the dangers of this virus.”

181.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
181.text: “Polio doesn't distinguish. It can infect you, your daughter, your son, your wife. Think about them.”

183.speaker: Player
183.text: “We don't have enough funds. I already told you my decision.”

184.speaker: Player
184.text: “When you put it that way...Very well. Procure whatever you need. [-1 Government Budget]”

185.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
185.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Media_Censored"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Media_Censored"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) == false)

187.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
187.text: “You will not regret this, Mr. President. I assure you.”

188.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
188.text: “You have once again proven that you are the right leader for Sordland in my eyes.”

191.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
191.text: “We need to implement a nationwide mandatory Polio vaccination policy.”

192.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
192.text: “With your order, I can immediately get to work to ensure we are doing whatever it takes.”

193.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
193.text: “This might seem excessive however, it is absolutely necessary.”

194.speaker: Player
194.text: “Whatever it takes to protect Sordland. Do it.”

195.speaker: Player
195.text: “Let's observe the situation first. We will be fine without it for now.”

196.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
196.text: “Very well. I will keep you up to date.”

198.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
198.text: “Now, if you will excuse me, I must get to work immediately.”

200.speaker: Narrator
200.text: He got up from his seat.

201.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
201.text: “That was it for today, Mr. President.”

203.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
203.text: “Thank you for your time, Mr. President.”

204.speaker: Narrator
204.text: He left my office, leaving me alone with a lot of paperwork to go through.

341.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
341.text: “Thank you for your time, Mr. President.”

389.text: “Thanks to the allocated funds from privatization, we have improved the healthcare in the country overall. I have used the resources to begin a comprehensive health reform.”
